programs.title: Agents Work, Members Govern: A Workshop for Aerospace and Technical Union Locals
outcomes: Explain the 'agents operate; people govern' division of labor in an agent-managed DAO
Identify which decisions (final votes, treasury, charter changes) stay in human hands
Draft a mock proposal in the Proposal Forum and carry it through human final vote
Assess how agent-managed coordination could affect worker voice and job quality

sessions.activity: Tour the charter and reserved-for-humans list; members map which governance powers can never be delegated to agents.
Compare agent-generated evidence summaries with traditional union research briefs; discuss trust, sourcing, and verification.
Small groups draft a workplace proposal with the Proposal & Grant Drafter's template, then debate and hold a human-only final vote.
Observe Task Router coordination of working groups; discuss how task routing affects workload, fairness, and representation.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized post-workshop survey responses on trust in agent-drafted materials and preferred human-reserved decision powers, contributed to shared education models.
programs.consent: Adult participants sign informed consent before the session; data is opt-in, de-identified, and participants may withdraw at any time with their contributions removed.

programs.title: Mission to 39A: Rockets, Wetlands, and Robot Helpers
outcomes: Locate Launch Complex 39A on a map and describe its wetland setting between the lagoon and the Atlantic
Describe what a DAO is and why some decisions are reserved for humans
Track a class 'mission' from proposal to vote using the zones of the world
Practice evaluating evidence summaries for accuracy and bias

sessions.activity: Students read a short Evidence Monitor-style summary about Kennedy Space Center and fact-check two claims against the brief's map facts.
Teams write a simple class proposal (e.g., a mock 'launch day plan') and vote on it themselves, learning that agents draft but people decide.
Discuss the mission 'AI governed as a public good'; students create a class charter listing decisions only humans should make.
Students build a progress tracker poster for their class mission and present it, mimicking the Progress Tracker agent's dashboard.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized class-level results (no individual names) such as aggregate quiz scores and charter ideas, contributed to shared civics-of-AI education models.
programs.consent: Written guardian/parent consent is required for all minors before participation; no personally identifiable information is collected, and guardians may opt out at any time.

programs.title: Governing AI as a Public Good: An NGO Field Study in an Agent-Managed DAO
programs.grade_or_level: Professional / NGO staff and program leads
outcomes: Analyze the AGI Future Foundation mission through the DAO's five-zone structure
Design a measurable-outcome framework for a public-good AI initiative
Facilitate a human-decision cycle where agents propose and people enact
Map collaboration opportunities using the Collaborator Scout workflow

sessions.activity: Workshop on translating mission statements into measurable charter outcomes; teams draft outcome indicators for an NGO program.
Practice commissioning and critiquing Research Synthesis Agent outputs; establish sourcing standards for NGO use.
Role-play working-group formation via the Task Router; identify experts and partners through a Collaborator Scout exercise.
Teams present full proposals drafted agent-style, then a human panel debates and takes the final vote — never the agents.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized outcome-indicator templates and proposal scoring rubrics, stripped of organization identifiers, contributed to shared NGO governance models.
programs.consent: Organizational memorandum of understanding plus individual consent for staff; all shared artifacts are de-identified and reviewed before contribution.

programs.title: From Pad 39A to Public Benefit: Nonprofit Governance in an Agent-Managed World
programs.grade_or_level: Nonprofit board members and senior staff
outcomes: Explain how agent-managed operations align with nonprofit fiduciary and stewardship duties
Distinguish agent-drafted proposals from human-only enactment, treasury, and windfall decisions
Build a board-level oversight checklist for agent-assisted programs
Evaluate progress reporting using the Progress Observatory model

sessions.activity: Board members compare the DAO charter's reserved human powers with nonprofit board duties; draft a stewardship map for their own organization.
Review sample agent-drafted grants and proposals; practice the human-only steps of debate, amendment, and enactment.
Audit a Progress Tracker dashboard; teams design measurable outcomes and reporting cadence for a nonprofit program.
Discuss task routing and working groups for lean nonprofit teams; identify where agent coordination helps and where human judgment must lead.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized governance checklists and oversight practices (no donor, beneficiary, or financial data) contributed to shared nonprofit governance models.
programs.consent: Individual consent forms for each participant; contributions are voluntary, aggregated, de-identified, and withdrawable on request.
